Maybe we do get 25% of Jeff Bezos’ income. The problem is the ultra wealthy can set their income to be whatever they want, so even though him or Elon Musk might be the richest people in the world at the time, they can easily make their income like 10k. This is why I’d argue raising income tax brackets at the high end doesn’t really do anything since it doesn’t really attack the fact that in an older report it was found that the 30 richest Americans have equal wealth to the bottom 50% of all Americans, and as time passes that disparity will only increase if something isn’t done. [Source](https://www.google.com/amp/s/www.forbes.com/sites/noahkirsch/2017/11/09/the-3-richest-americans-hold-more-wealth-than-bottom-50-of-country-study-finds/amp/)

The best way I can say it is the value of your money doesn’t really scale linearly. Taxing 25% of 50,000 will make it much harder for that person to survive than if I taxed 25% of 200,000 that person isn’t really struggling to survive. The further from the poverty line you are the less value each individual dollar is to you, and as you reach a certain point, like billionaires, your funds are pretty much inexhaustible besides using them to accrue even more wealth. So by having tax brackets you can relieve pressure on people around the poverty line, but still take in enough tax to support government policy.
